scope: Retrospective theorem-directed algebra, with no new points or parameter search.
hypothesis: Shared first norm-conic solubility distinguishes the previously fixed chain classes or the soluble anchor from its obstructed deformations.
checks: Construct norm witnesses for all twenty retained anchor basis classes and the three fixed chain masks.
Transport the norm witnesses across the seven retained models without solving a new conic.
Verify the translated cubic, the rational 2-isogeny coefficients over the cubic field, and the constant quadratic discriminant class.
Use restriction-corestriction to distinguish cubic base change from passage to the full splitting field.
Check whether the simplest transported anchor norm point retains rational x-coordinate.
limits: Only cubic arithmetic, 23 norm witnesses, seven existing parameters, and 140 exact coordinate identities. No field/class-group computation, descent campaign, conic search, or point search.
failure_semantics: Universally soluble norm conics refute their use as a discriminator. They do not imply that the associated isogeny quartics or rational 2-covers have points.
oracle_boundary: Anchor points are used only for labelled retrospective norm witnesses; no prospective selector receives them.
